slot.brief: Show/verify which of the statement forms (~(p∧q)) → r, (p→r)∨(q→r) etc. are logically equivalent by truth table or algebraic manipulation; pick the equivalent pair.

stem: Which pair of compound propositions is logically equivalent for every truth assignment to $p,q,r$?

verdicts.working: A: Both propositions simplify to (p∧q)∨r. B, C, and D are not equivalent pairs.

working:
$[\sim(p\wedge q)]\Rightarrow r\equiv(p\wedge q)\vee r$; $\sim[(p\Rightarrow\sim q)\wedge\sim r]\equiv\sim[(\sim p\vee\sim q)\wedge\sim r]\equiv(p\wedge q)\vee r$

Independent check: A: Both propositions simplify to (p∧q)∨r. B, C, and D are not equivalent pairs.
solution:
Using $a\Rightarrow b\equiv\sim a\vee b$,
$$[\sim(p\wedge q)]\Rightarrow r\equiv(p\wedge q)\vee r.$$
Also, $\sim[(p\Rightarrow\sim q)\wedge\sim r]\equiv\sim[(\sim p\vee\sim q)\wedge\sim r]\equiv(p\wedge q)\vee r$; hence the pair in (D) is equivalent.
